correctness.rationale: A distributional BV derivative is a finite signed measure. After mean subtraction the centered Heaviside representation is exact; the first-moment condition becomes a strictly positive h-weight cancellation. Jordan decomposition and product coupling express every admissible derivative as a positive-weight average of normalized signed two-point derivatives, with total weights exactly |Df|. The L2 triangle inequality proves the bound; every two-point profile is admissible, giving sharpness. Covariance yields K; compactness and vanishing at boundary give an attained maximum. For uniform weight K=H(s)H(t)d(1-d)/(H(s)+H(t))², and two elementary sharp factor bounds plus an exact nonnegative deficit classify the unique optimizing jump sites. Equality in the coupled upper bound forces the signed derivative to these sites. The bundled rational checker confirms 1764 finite identities but is not the proof.

value.rationale: Two independent moment constraints are natural when data are detrended against affine signals. The complete weighted coefficient reduces an infinite-dimensional constrained BV extremal problem to an explicit two-parameter covariance maximum, while the unweighted case gives the exact 1/4 sharp norm and a unique spatially localized three-level equality pattern with a nonnegative defect identity. This is a structural bound for detrended signals, not a mere reformulation of ordinary single-mean Poincare or a computed arbitrary sample.
